notes: §1985:VI.6.23.3 SR2: "Identifier-1 and identifier-2 must each reference an index data item or an elementary item described as an integer" (an integer item has no digit positions right of the decimal point, §1985:III.2). Identifier-1 is SetBinder.ScreenIndexAssignmentReceiver's OperandClassScreen row (COBOL2326 for a PIC 9V9, SVPP9, edited, alphanumeric, group or reference-modified receiver, also inside a receiver list); identifier-2 is IndexAssignmentSenderOf (COBOL2326 for edited, alphanumeric, group) plus the 85-only GateCobol85IndexAmount/IsCobol85IndexAmount, which refuses a scaled numeric sender (the witness's PIC 9V9, SVPP9) and any function or expression with COBOL0900, a refusal --std 2002 lifts. Probes at 85: index data item, signed S9(4), 9(18), COMP, COMP-3, 9PP, a subscripted table integer and an ODO-table index all accepted and run with correct values; N(1:1) COBOL0844; an unsubscripted table element COBOL2270.

next.reason: Identifier-1 is kept: §2023:14.9.39.3 SR1 'shall reference a data item of class index or an integer data item'. Identifier-2 narrows: §2023:14.9.39.3 SR2 'shall reference a data item of class index'. The 1985 integer sender is now written as arithmetic-expression-1 (§2023:14.9.39.2), which no syntax rule requires to be an integer. Instead §2023:14.9.39.4 GR2 sets EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT 'If the value of arithmetic-expression-1 does not result in an integer'. A non-integer numeric sender, refused at compile time in 1985, compiles and raises a run-time exception condition (error mode c).
